Class CreativeSlotWrapper

java.lang.Object
net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot
com.trevlar.menukit.core.CreativeSlotWrapper
All Implemented Interfaces:
com.trevlar.menukit.mixin.SlotWrapperAccessor
public final class CreativeSlotWrapper extends net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot implements com.trevlar.menukit.mixin.SlotWrapperAccessor
A library-built stand-in for vanilla's package-private CreativeModeInventoryScreen$SlotWrapper, used to carry a registered MKCSlot into the creative non-inventory tabs so it draws and routes there exactly as it does on the inventory tab (§0051 creative parity, extended to all tabs).

Why a custom wrapper

Vanilla only wraps player.inventoryMenu's slots — slots included — into the ItemPickerMenu on the inventory tab; the non-inventory tabs carry a fixed base slot set (the item grid + hotbar) that never sees the slot, so a slot is invisible and unclickable there. We append one of these wrappers per slot to that base set (MKCCreativeSlotItemPickerMixin) so the existing slot dispatch — which walks menu.slots and unwraps via Slots.target(Slot) — discovers the slot on every tab. We can't construct vanilla's SlotWrapper (package-private), so this mirrors its delegation and, crucially, implements the same SlotWrapperAccessor unwrap seam MenuKit applies to vanilla's wrapper — so Slots.target/MKCSlotAccess.asMKCSlot resolve it to the slot with no special case.

Parked, like the inventory-tab wrappers

Constructed off-screen (the screen dispatcher draws the slot at its live renderX/renderY instead), and its placement clicks are re-routed to the proven inventory-tab path by MKCCreativeSlotClickRouteMixin. The delegation below keeps vanilla's own reads/writes (item, may-place, take, etc.) faithful for anything that does touch the wrapper directly.

No client types — universal-safe — though only the client creative path ever constructs it.
